title: Senior Counsel, Privacy & Product (Hybrid)
description: <p><strong>Location: </strong>London, UK – Hybrid (2 days per week in office)</p> <p>With millions of diners, 70,000+ restaurant partners and 25+ years of experience, OpenTable, part of Booking Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an industry leader with a passion for helping restaurants thrive. Our world-class technology empowers restaurants to focus on what matters most – their team, their guests, and their bottom line – while enabling diners to discover and book the perfect restaurant for every occasion. </p> <p>Every employee at OpenTable has a tangible impact on what we do and how we do it. You’ll also be part of a global team that includes and its portfolio of metasearch brands. Hospitality is all about taking care of others, and it defines our culture.</p> <p><strong>About the job</strong><strong><br></strong>OpenTable is looking for a highly motivated, practical, and business-oriented Senior Counsel, Privacy & Product to join our Legal team. You will serve as a trusted advisor to OpenTable’s Product, Engineering, Security, Commercial, Partnerships, and Marketing teams, providing strategic and practical counsel across product development, privacy and data protection, artificial intelligence, information security, consumer protection, and related regulatory matters. You will also serve as OpenTable’s Deputy Privacy Officer, helping lead and operationalize OpenTable’s global privacy program and serving as a key liaison with Booking Holdings, Inc. (BHI) on privacy and data protection matters. This role is ideal for a lawyer who enjoys working closely with commercial, product and technical teams, navigating emerging areas of law, and developing practical solutions that enable responsible innovation at scale.</p> <p><strong>Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as a primary legal partner to OpenTable’s Product, Engineering, Security, Commercial, Partnerships, and Marketing teams, providing end-to-end counseling on new products, features, data uses, integrations, consumer experiences, and other strategic initiatives.</li> <li>Serve as Deputy Privacy Officer for OpenTable, helping lead and operationalize OpenTable’s global privacy program and serving as a key liaison with BHI on privacy strategy, governance, regulatory developments, and group-wide privacy initiatives.</li> <li>Advise on global privacy and data protection requirements and embed privacy-by-design principles into OpenTable’s products and operations, including counseling on data collection, use, sharing, retention, consent, personalization, and consumer rights.</li> <li>Provide strategic legal guidance on the development, deployment, procurement, and use of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, including generative AI and AI-powered product features, and help develop scalable AI governance frameworks as the regulatory landscape evolves.</li> <li>Provide strategic legal advice and guidance to Product teams regarding product development, launch, and sunsetting, with strong focus on legal risks related to data privacy, cybersecurity, data usage and ownership, consumer protection, and marketing. </li> <li>Partner closely with OpenTable’s Information Security team on cybersecurity and data security matters, including product and vendor security risk, security requirements, incident response, potential data breaches, regulatory obligations, and remediation.</li> <li>Identify and address emerging product, privacy, AI, security, consumer protection, and regulatory risks; draft and negotiate related agreements and terms; and develop scalable legal processes, policies, playbooks, and disclosures that enable the business to innovate responsibly.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Minimum Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>8+ years of relevant legal experience, including significant experience advising on privacy, data protection, technology, and product matters, preferably in-house at a technology, consumer, marketplace, or other high-growth company.</li> <li>J.D. from an accredited U.S. law school and active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar, or equivalent legal qualification and authorization to practice law in the United Kingdom.</li> <li>Deep knowledge of U.S. and global privacy and data protection laws, including GDPR and U.S. state privacy laws, as well as global consumer protection laws, with demonstrated experience translating complex legal and regulatory requirements into practical product and business guidance.</li> <li>Significant experience providing product counseling, including partnering directly with Product and Engineering teams on new products, features, data uses, and technology initiatives from development through launch.</li> <li>Experience supporting or helping lead a global privacy program, including privacy governance, policies, compliance frameworks, and cross-functional implementation.</li> <li>Experience advising on information security and cybersecurity matters, including security requirements, incident response, and related regulatory obligations.</li> <li>Strong judgment, communication, and stakeholder-management skills, with demonstrated ability to assess risk, navigate ambiguity, and provide practical advice to cross-functional teams and senior leaders.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Preferred Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience advising on artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, including legal and regulatory considerations associated with developing, deploying, or procuring AI-enabled products and services.</li> <li>Experience working within a complex global organization or corporate group and partnering effectively with enterprise-level legal, privacy, security, compliance, or governance functions.</li> <li>CIPP/US, CIPP/E, CIPM, AIGP, or similar privacy or AI certification preferred.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>Benefits and Perks</strong></h4> <ul> <li>5 weeks paid vacation</li> <li>Private health & dental insurance</li> <li>Work from (almost) anywhere for up to 20 days per year</li> <li>Focus on mental health and well-being:</li> <ul> <li>Company-paid therapy sessions through SpringHealth</li> <li>Company-paid subscription to Headspace</li> <li>Annual company-wide week off a year - the whole team fully recharges (and returns without a pile-up of work!)</li> </ul> <li>Paid parental leave</li> <li>Time off for your birthday</li> <li>Paid volunteer time</li> <li>Focus on your career growth:</li> <ul> <li>Development Dollars</li> <li>Leadership development</li> <li>Access to thousands of on-demand e-learnings</li> </ul> <li>Travel Discounts</li> <li>Employee Resource Groups</li> <li>Income protection and life assurance</li> <li>Employee Assistance Program - including 24/7 GP & free legal advice</li> <li>Pension plan contributions</li> <li>Discounted gym membership</li> <li>Bike2Work</li> <li>Season ticket loan</li> <li>Social events & Thursday happy hours</li> <li>Free lunch 2 days per week</li> </ul> <p>The best connections happen face-to-face, whether you’re sitting down to dinner or having coffee with a coworker. That’s why OpenTable has adopted a hybrid workplace model. This role aligns with that approach, with an expectation of coming into the office two days a week—giving employees the best of both worlds: in-person collaboration and flexibility.</p> <p><strong>Work Environment & Flexibility</strong></p> <p>At OpenTable, we pride ourselves on fostering a global and dynamic work environment. As a team member with us, you will benefit from a schedule tailored to accommodate a global workforce operating across multiple time zones. While the majority of your responsibilities may align with conventional business hours, there will be instances where you are expected to manage communications - via calls, Slack messages, or emails - outside of regular working hours to effectively collaborate with international colleagues, respond to restaurant partners, and/or address urgent matters. OpenTable will always abide by and consider local laws and regulations.</p> <p><strong>Inclusion</strong></p> <p>We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels they belong and can thrive. We know the best ideas come when we bring different voices to the table, so we're building a team as dynamic as the diners and restaurants we serve—and fostering a culture where everyone feels welcome to be themselves.</p> <p>If you need any reasonable adjustments during the application/interview process, or on the job, we’re here to support you. Please reach out to your recruiter to request any accommodations.</p> <p>#LI-BR1</p> <p>#LI-Hybrid</p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Enterprise Account Executive - Spanish -Speaking  - London, UK
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>About Pallet </strong></p> <p class="isSelectedEnd">Pallet is building AI Agents to transform the physical economy — a $12 trillion global industry. We’ve raised $50M from top investors, including General Catalyst, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures. In under two years, we’ve achieved 700% revenue growth and are just getting started.</p> <p class="isSelectedEnd">Our mission is to increase the efficiency of the global supply chain by automating the manual workflows that slow supply chain teams down — from scheduling and appointment setting to data entry and load management. Our flagship platform provides end-to-end visibility, control, and optimization, while our newest product, CoPallet, introduces AI Agents that can understand and execute requests in real time and integrate directly with customer systems.</p> <p class="isSelectedEnd">As companies across the physical economy look to generative AI to drive efficiency, many are turning to Pallet to lead the way. With deep supply chain expertise and cutting-edge AI capabilities, we’re positioned to build the next $10B company powering the physical economy.</p> <p>Join us and work alongside leaders from Google, DoorDash, YC, and more to shape the future of supply chain technology.</p></div><p><strong>London, United Kingdom or Zurich, Switzerland (Remote to start, transitioning to 5 days/week in-office once our local office opens)</strong></p> <p><strong>You could be an Enterprise Account Executive anywhere. Why us?</strong></p> <ul> <li>Join a well-funded, high-growth startup on a clear path to $100M ARR.</li> <li>Sell a category-defining AI Agents platform with massive surface area across logistics.</li> <li>Build Pallet’s presence across Europe as one of the first commercial hires on the ground.</li> <li>Work directly with founders and senior leadership to define our international go-to-market strategy.</li> <li>Help transform one of the world’s largest industries while building toward a $10B+ outcome.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the opportunity</strong></p> <p>We’re hiring our first Enterprise Account Executives in EMEA to build Pallet’s commercial presence across Europe.</p> <p>You’ll own net-new enterprise acquisition across the region, build relationships with the largest logistics providers in Europe, and help establish the playbook for our international expansion. This is a highly consultative enterprise sales role focused on educating customers on an entirely new category of AI-powered workflow automation.</p> <p>You’ll partner closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Solutions, and Customer Success to drive a solution-selling motion centered around workflow discovery, AI use case identification, structured pilots, and measurable ROI.</p> <p>Initially, this role will be remote from London while we establish our UK presence. Once our London office opens, this role will transition to working from the office five days per week when not traveling to customer sites.</p> <p><strong>How you will make an impact</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own the full enterprise sales cycle across EMEA, from outbound prospecting through contract signature.</li> <li>Build and maintain a 3x-4x qualified pipeline through disciplined outbound execution while self-sourcing at least 30% of opportunities.</li> <li>Develop relationships with executive stakeholders across Europe’s largest logistics providers, including COO, CIO, VP Operations, VP Supply Chain, and VP Technology.</li> <li>Lead consultative discovery sessions that map operational workflows to Pallet’s AI agent capabilities.</li> <li>Scope and lead structured pilots that demonstrate measurable operational ROI and convert into enterprise deployments.</li> <li>Build executive business cases that align operational improvements with financial outcomes.</li> <li>Document repeatable customer use cases and market feedback to shape Pallet’s product roadmap and international GTM strategy.</li> <li>Help establish Pallet as the leading AI platform for enterprise logistics across Europe.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What we’re looking for</strong></p> <ul> <li>8+ years of enterprise B2B SaaS or enterprise logistics sales experience.</li> <li>Business-fluent Spanish you can run discovery, negotiate and present to executives in Spanish. </li> <li>Proven track record of consistently closing six- and seven-figure enterprise software agreements.</li> <li>Strong consultative selling and value-based sales methodology.</li> <li>Experience navigating complex buying committees and long enterprise sales cycles.</li> <li>Executive presence with senior operators and technology leaders.</li> <li>Comfortable selling technical, workflow-heavy software products.</li> <li>Ability to quickly understand complex logistics operations and translate them into compelling AI automation opportunities.</li> <li>Excellent outbound prospecting and territory-building discipline.</li> <li>Willingness to travel extensively across Europe.</li> </ul> <p>Experience selling into logistics, supply chain, transportation, or warehouse operations is strongly preferred but not required. Candidates without logistics experience should demonstrate an ability to quickly learn operational workflows and become trusted advisors to customers.</p> <p><strong>Working model</strong></p> <p>Working hours are generally <strong>9:00am-6:00pm London time</strong>, providing full coverage of the European business day while maintaining regular collaboration with our San Francisco headquarters.</p> <p>You’ll typically spend:</p> <ul> <li>Mornings and early afternoons working directly with European customers and prospects.</li> <li>Late afternoons collaborating with our US-based Sales, Product, and Engineering teams during our daily overlap window.</li> <li>Approximately 75% of your time traveling across Europe for customer meetings, executive workshops, pilots, and industry events.</li> </ul> <p>Initially this role will be remote. Once Pallet opens its local office, you’ll work from the office five days per week whenever you’re not traveling to customers.</p> <p><strong>Reporting structure</strong></p> <p>You’ll report directly to the <strong>General Manager, London</strong> for territory strategy, customer relationships, and international expansion.</p> <p>You’ll also work closely with our <strong>Head of Sales</strong>, participating in weekly pipeline reviews, forecasting, and sales process alignment with the US team.</p> <p><strong>Interview Process</strong></p> <ul> <li>Chat with Christy - Business Recruiter - 30 mins</li> <li>Deal Review - 30 mins</li> <li>Discovery Mock Interview - 45-60 mins</li> <li>Final Interview - ~3 hours</li> <li>Brief Background Check and Reference Check</li> </ul> <p>We move fast, and we’ll keep you informed at every stage of the process.</p> <p><strong>Compensation</strong></p> <p>The estimated compensation range for this role is <strong>£100,000-£240,000 OTE</strong>, depending on experience and skill set.</p> <p>Our compensation follows a standard 50/50 enterprise sales structure consisting of base salary and target commission. High performers are eligible for uncapped commission accelerators above quota.</p> <p>In addition to cash compensation, we offer competitive equity, benefits, and significant growth opportunities as one of our earliest international commercial hires.</p> <p>Final compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and demonstrated enterprise sales performance.</p> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Our Benefits </strong></p> <p>We invest in our people the same way we invest in our product: seriously.</p> <ul> <li>🩺 Health, Vision, and Dental benefits </li> <li>🏝️ Take-what-you-need Paid Vacation</li> <li>➕ Life Insurance and Accidental Insurance </li> <li>❤️‍🩹 Short-Term Disability Coverage</li> <li>💸 Generous salary and equity for all staff</li> <li>🪜 401k option; helping you save for the future</li> <li>🧑‍🧑‍🧒‍🧒 Paid parental leave to support growing families</li> <li>📚 Yearly learning and development stipend</li> <li>🚌 Commuter benefits for Bay Area employees</li> <li>🚘 Uber ride stipend if you ever have to work late in the office </li> <li>🏡 Remote office home stipend to get you comfy in your space</li> <li>🍔 Daily catered lunches provided </li> <li>✈️ Onboarding trip to San Francisco HQ if you work remotely</li> <li>🥤 Monthly happy hours</li> <li>🎉 Annual Company Offsites; our last one was in Palm Springs CA 🌴</li> </ul> <p><strong>Workplace Policy</strong></p> <p>We are an in-person company. Our offices in San Francisco, New York City and London are where ideas get built, decisions get made, and the team gets stronger. We have invested in making them genuinely great places to spend your day, with catered lunches, monthly happy hours, and people who care about the work and each other.</p> <p>Most of our team works in office five days a week. For select roles, we hire remotely across the U.S. Remote employees come to one of our offices for their first week to onboard and meet the team, and we cover the full trip. </p> <p>Every role is different. Travel expectations are always shared upfront in the job description and confirmed in your first call with us.</p> <p><strong>Equal Opportunity</strong></p> <p>Pallet is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We make all employment decisions based solely on merit. We provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees without discrimination on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, disability status, or any other applicable legally protected characteristic. We prohibit any form of discrimination or harassment. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including hiring.</p> <p><strong>Candidate Privacy Notice</strong></p> <p>Please review Pallet’s Candidate Privacy Notice <a href="https://pallet.com/privacy">here</a>.</p> <p><strong>Accommodations</strong></p> <p>Pallet complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), as amended by the ADA Amendments Act, and all applicable state or local laws. The role Checkout.com is looking for an enthusiastic Engineer I to join Finance Technology with a focus on Workday Adaptive Planning . Adaptive Planning supports finance, workforce, sales, and operational planning, giving teams a shared platform for budgeting, forecasting, modelling, reporting, and decision-making. This is an early-career engineering role for someone who wants to build depth in finance systems, application configuration, data integration, and operational support. You will work with Finance, Finance Technology, Data, and wider Corporate Technology teams to keep planning processes reliable, well-controlled, and easy to operate. You will have support from more senior engineers for complex design decisions, but you will be expected to work independently for longer periods on well-defined configuration, integration, support, and continuous-improvement tasks. This reflects Checkout’s Engineer 1 expectations: delivering small-to-medium-sized work, supporting common operational flows, communicating clearly, and taking ownership of the quality of what you deliver. How you’ll make an impact Configure, maintain, and enhance Adaptive Planning models, dimensions, versions, levels, accounts, sheets, reports, dashboards, and planning workflows under appropriate guidance. Support the delivery of budgeting, forecasting, headcount planning, scenario modelling, and management reporting capabilities for Finance and business stakeholders. Build and support data loads and integrations between Adaptive Planning, Workday Financials, Workday HCM, and other approved internal or third-party systems. Maintain data mappings, transformation rules, validation checks, and reconciliation processes so that planning data is complete, accurate, and traceable. Monitor scheduled loads and integration tasks, investigate failures, and resolve common data or configuration issues within agreed service levels. Triage incidents and service requests, identifying root causes and escalating complex or high-risk issues with clear evidence and recommended next steps. Partner with Finance stakeholders to understand requirements and translate them into maintainable system configuration, reporting, or integration changes. Contribute to the assessment and delivery of future analytics data flows, including the potential use of Adaptive Planning data in BigQuery and management analytics. Participate in testing, regression testing, release preparation, and controlled deployment of Adaptive Planning changes. Follow change-control, access-management, data-quality, and audit requirements relevant to financial systems and planning data. Create clear documentation, support guides, data dictionaries, integration runbooks, and knowledge-base articles so that operational knowledge is shared rather than held by one person. Identify recurring manual work or failure patterns and propose practical automation and process improvements. What we’re looking for Essential experience and skills Experience in a finance systems, enterprise applications, data, reporting, or integration environment. Practical experience with Workday Adaptive Planning, or strong experience with a comparable planning, performance-management, ERP, or finance application and a clear ability to learn Adaptive quickly. Understanding of core finance planning concepts such as budgets, forecasts, actuals, variance analysis, allocations, dimensions, hierarchies, and scenarios. Experience configuring or supporting structured data models, application workflows, reports, dashboards, or business rules. Ability to work with data imports, exports, mappings, transformations, validations, and reconciliations. Strong troubleshooting skills, with the ability to break down an issue, gather evidence, identify likely causes, and communicate findings clearly. Good attention to detail and an understanding of why accuracy, access control, auditability, and repeatability matter in finance systems. Ability to manage small-to-medium-sized tasks independently while knowing when to ask for help or escalate. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with Finance and Technology stakeholders. Desirable experience Workday Adaptive Planning certification or implementation experience. Experience with Adaptive Planning Integration, Planning Data Loader, APIs, or equivalent enterprise planning integration tooling. Experience integrating planning systems with Workday Financials, Workday HCM, an ERP, a data warehouse, or a reporting platform. Familiarity with SOX controls, financial audit requirements, data privacy, and segregation of duties. Experience supporting month-end, budget, forecast, or management-reporting cycles. Exposure to Agile delivery, ticket-driven change management, incident management, or service-management practices. Diagnose and resolve routine integration or data-quality issues using a structured troubleshooting approach. Deliver small-to-medium-sized enhancements from requirement clarification through testing, documentation, and controlled release. Explain key planning data flows, mappings, dependencies, and operational controls to Finance and Technology colleagues. Improve the reliability or efficiency of at least one recurring planning or finance-technology process. Maintain accurate, useful documentation and contribute positively to team ceremonies, reviews, and knowledge-sharing sessions. Working style and behaviours We are looking for someone who: Takes ownership of tasks and follows through on commitments. Acts with urgency and accountability when issues affect Finance or business reporting. Is curious about how finance processes, data, and technology fit together. Communicates clearly, especially when explaining risk, blockers, trade-offs, or support impact. Welcomes feedback and actively develops their technical and domain knowledge. Collaborates generously and shares knowledge so the team does not depend on a single subject-matter expert. Looks for durable automation and simpler operating processes rather than repeatedly working around the same manual problem. Why join Finance Technology? You will work on systems that sit at the centre of how Checkout.com plans, forecasts, reports, and makes financial decisions. The role offers the opportunity to develop a broad foundation across enterprise applications, finance processes, integrations, data quality, controls, and automation while working closely with experienced Finance and Technology professionals. He's direct, so you'll always know exactly where you stand, and he expects that same directness back: if you disagree, he wants the pushback, backed by data, not silence. Sharpen process and tooling. You'll help spot where the team's workflows and tooling could run more efficiently, and support the Senior Manager in rolling out improvements without stripping reps of their autonomy. You'll be the go-to person for best practice on Salesforce, Outreach, and the team's automation tools. Contribute to the wider GTM motion. You'll keep strong alignment with your AE partners and take part in pipe review cadences. You'll support the Senior Manager in preparing performance updates and regional insights, and join bi-weekly RD cadences where it makes sense. WHAT YOU'LL BRING Hands-on ADR or SDR experience. You know what this job feels like from the inside, not just what it looks like from a deck. A real coach's instinct. You get energy from making other people better, not just from hitting your own number. The ability to juggle competing priorities without dropping the ball. Your own quota, coaching newer reps, and process work will all pull on your time in the same week, and you know how to decide what actually matters right now. Strong time management. This is one we screen for directly, not something we assume comes with experience. A bias for building. You spot what needs fixing and go build it, rather than working only through a list of tasks someone else handed you. Analytical rigor. You make calls based on data, not gut feel, and you're comfortable being specific about why a number moved, including when that number is going the wrong way. A track record of top-tier performance that holds up on both counts: the day-to-day discipline that drives it (activity, sequence execution, pipeline hygiene), and the results that discipline produces, quarter over quarter, not just once. Real trust with your AE and RD partners, earned through consistency, not just alignment on paper. Transparency, especially with leadership, especially when something isn't on track. We'd rather hear it early than find out later. The kind of presence the team actually looks up to, not just reports to. Comfort in an allbound model with a heavy outbound emphasis. Self-awareness and a genuine investment in growing as a leader. Language skills relevant to the UK, Benelux, or Nordics are a bonus, not a requirement. Energy and intention every day. Every challenge is a chance to get stronger. Character. Good humans first. Integrity, humility, and keeping our word. Together. No one gets left behind. Differences make us better, not harder to manage. Truth. Radical honesty. We say the hard things with care. That's how we move fast. Accountable. We own our results, bias toward action, and don't wait to be told. Pioneering. We take up space, experiment, and bring creative thinking to every challenge. In NEMEA specifically, we operate in mature markets. We don't manufacture urgency, we earn entry by knowing the landscape better than the prospect does. description: Build a Safer World. TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure. About the role TRM is building a highly impactful, collaborative Environmental Crimes intelligence function, with one goal: disrupt the illicit actors behind wildlife trafficking and other environmental crimes, and add real friction to their ability to operate. As our Senior or Staff Intelligence Analyst, Environmental Crimes , you will own TRM's intelligence on this category end-to-end. You will research, analyze, and publish intelligence on environmental crime networks and the crypto and financial flows behind them, combining on-chain tracing, OSINT, and off-chain data from partners into a picture that law enforcement, NGOs, and private-sector partners can act on. You will also be the clear TRM owner for our partnership with United for Wildlife and Project Pangolin, serving a global network of partner organizations as a trusted advisor, convener, and the expert user who shapes how TRM's products serve this mission. What makes this role unique: you get to build a new intelligence category from the ground up, on the leading blockchain intelligence platform, with executive sponsorship and direct real-world impact. The impact you will have Build the environmental crimes threat picture. Research, author, and publish intelligence products (threat assessments, typology reports, trend analysis, actor profiles, network maps) on environmental crime and the illicit finance behind it, and maintain a reusable threat picture inside TRM's intelligence infrastructure. Drive investigations to action. Develop and use a wide variety of intelligence sources, tools, and capabilities — on-chain, OSINT, and partner-provided off-chain data — to identify the wallets, entities, and off-ramps behind environmental crime networks. Produce structured, source-cited targeting packages that support law enforcement and partner investigations and surface disruption opportunities. Own the United for Wildlife partner program. Replace fractional coverage with a managed, repeatable program across a network of 200+ partner organizations: case assistance, analysis, guidance, training, and onboarding. Bring the community together. Organize virtual and in-person cross-sector, cross-border sprints and working groups aimed at real-time disruption, and collaborate with partners such as USFWS, HSI, DOJ, Interpol, UNODC, national agencies, and NGOs. Be TRM's public voice on environmental crimes. Brief internal stakeholders, partners, and leadership, and represent TRM with media, at external events, and with other stakeholders to amplify our intelligence. Shape the product. Act as the representative power user of TRM's mission tooling for the environmental crimes community, turning field needs into structured feedback and partnering with product teams to prototype new analysis and collaboration capabilities. Scale your coverage with AI. Build reusable AI workflows for signal processing, target selection, and drafting, with human validation where it matters, so more of your time goes to high-judgment analysis and partner delivery. What we're looking for 5+ years in intelligence analysis, financial crime, illicit finance, blockchain intelligence, or transnational threat investigations. Domain knowledge of wildlife trafficking, environmental crime, and/or transnational smuggling — or a closely adjacent illicit-trade domain, with a demonstrated ability to ramp fast. Proven ability to independently run complex, multi-source investigations and produce clear, decision-ready, source-cited written intelligence for both expert and non-expert audiences. Strong proficiency in OSINT methodology and tradecraft, with hands-on experience using commercial databases and investigative tools. Production AI fluency: you already use AI and LLMs to accelerate research and analysis, build reusable workflows, and critically evaluate AI output — neither accept-all nor reject-all. A partner- and community-facing operator: you build trust and energize a multi-organization network, and you are comfortable owning an external partner program, not only heads-down analysis. What are you waiting for?</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"201341983":0,"335551550":1,"335551620":1,"335559685":0,"335559737":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":279}"> </span></p></div><p> </p> <p><strong>Life at THG Nutrition</strong></p> <p> </p> <p data-start="353" data-end="578">THG Nutrition is home to some of the world’s most trusted and best-loved wellbeing and nutrition brands, including Myprotein, the world’s largest online sports nutrition brand, alongside Myvegan, Myvitamins and MP Activewear.</p> <p data-start="580" data-end="776">Our brands and people exist to break boundaries — to power and empower those who want more. We move fast, challenge convention, and back ourselves to win. These values shape how we work every day.</p> <p> </p> <p><strong>Role: Category Manager | Bars & Snacks</strong></p> <p><strong>Reporting to: Category Director</strong></p> <p><strong>Brand: Myprotein</strong></p> <p><strong>Location: THG HQ, Manchester (WA15 0AF) - Fully Office Based</strong></p> <p><strong>THG Nutrition:</strong></p> <p>THG Nutrition is home to some of the best loved and most trusted names in wellbeing and nutrition, including Myprotein, the world's largest online sports nutrition brand, and its family of brands,  Myvitamins and MP Activewear. Our brands and people exist to break boundaries; to power and empower those who want more.</p> <p><strong>Role Overview</strong></p> <p>As the Category Manager, you will be responsible for driving the online commercial success of Bars & Snacks. You will optimise the ecommerce strategy for these categories, ensuring commercial growth and customer engagement across global markets in line with out omni-channel business.</p> <p><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></p> <p><em><strong>Category Performance & Strategy</strong></em></p> <ul> <li>Develop and implement bars & snacks strategies to maximise online sales, market share, and profitability.</li> <li>Analyse internal insights (sales data, pricing trends, site metrics) to make data-driven decisions that optimise category performance.</li> <li>Identify category growth opportunities, leveraging global and regional insights to tailor strategies for each market.</li> <li>Conduct frequent site audits to ensure optimal customer experience (CX) and category visibility.</li> </ul> <p><em><strong>Market & Competitor Analysis</strong></em></p> <ul> <li>Monitor external market trends, including competitor pricing, innovation, and emerging category trends.</li> <li>Leverage insights to develop category plans and influence product launches, pricing, and promotional strategies.</li> <li>Collaborate with the Brand & Marketing teams to align product positioning with industry trends and customer demand.</li> <li>Collaborate with the internal Retail, Wholesale, Tiktok & Amazon teams to understand insights & omnichannel sales to drive online decisions.</li> </ul> <p><em><strong>Pricing & Promotion Optimisation</strong></em></p> <ul> <li>Own the pricing strategy for assigned categories, ensuring profitability while remaining competitive in each market.</li> <li>Work closely with country managers to optimise pricing across Myprotein sites, balancing growth and margin targets.</li> <li>Work closely with the internal Retail, Wholesale, Tiktok & Amazon teams to balance the calendar plans to drive growth across channels</li> <li>Develop and implement promotional plans, working with digital marketing teams to drive customer acquisition and retention.</li> </ul> <p><em><strong>Cross-Functional Collaboration</strong></em></p> <ul> <li>Partner with supply chain & production teams to ensure optimal stock availability across all international warehouses.</li> <li>Collaborate with procurement, finance & logistics to improve cost efficiencies and bottom-line profitability.</li> <li>Support senior stakeholders in optimising locale & sales channels mix, reducing cost prices, and managing discount strategies.</li> <li>Work closely with customer service teams to address category-specific customer concerns, ensuring a customer-centric approach to category management.</li> </ul> <p><em><strong>Performance Tracking & Reporting</strong></em></p> <ul> <li>Establish and maintain reporting processes to track category performance at a territory level.</li> <li>Present insights and strategic recommendations to senior leadership and key stakeholders.</li> <li>Continuously monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and adjust strategies accordingly to drive category success.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What We’re Looking For</strong></p> <ul> <li>Proven experience in Ecommerce, Category Management, or Digital Trading, ideally within retail, FMCG, or nutrition/bars & snacks sectors.</li> <li>Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data and translate insights into actionable strategies.</li> <li>Commercial mindset with experience in pricing, promotion, and margin optimisation.</li> <li>Ability to build strong cross-functional relationships and influence stakeholders across marketing, finance, supply chain, and country teams.</li> <li>Detail-oriented with a strong understanding of customer experience (CX) and ecommerce best practices.</li> <li>Proficiency in analytics tools (e.g., BI platforms i.e. Tableau) and ecommerce platforms.</li> <li>Strong organisational and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.</li> <li>Proficiency in excel, SQL & Ai Tools would be desirable as well, but not essential</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><span What are you waiting for?</span><span data-ccp-props="{"134233117":false,"134233118":false,"201341983":0,"335551550":1,"335551620":1,"335559685":0,"335559737":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":279}"> </span></p></div><p><strong><span data-contrast="none">Location: Omega, WA5 3TP (3 days) / Icon 1, WA15 0AF (1 day) / WFH (1 day)</span></strong></p> <p><strong><span data-contrast="none">About THG Manufacturing</span></strong></p> <p><strong>THG Manufacturing</strong> is the dedicated, high-growth contract manufacturing and co-manufacturing division of THG PLC. Operating from state-of-the-art, BRCGS-accredited manufacturing facilities globally, we partner with prestigious household names and global powerhouse brands who trust us to formulate, produce, and scale their product ranges.</p> <p>Our specialised manufacturing capabilities include:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Powder Blending</strong> (sports nutrition, lifestyle powders, functional health formulations)</li> <li><strong>Tablets & Capsules</strong> (vitamins, minerals, and dietary supplements)</li> <li><strong>Protein Bar Manufacturing</strong> (extruded, layered, and premium enrobed formats)</li> <li><strong>Fruit Preparations & Concentrates</strong> (aseptic processing and clean-label infusions)</li> </ul> <p><strong>An Unrivaled Growth Trajectory</strong></p> <p>This is an exceptional time to join our division. THG Manufacturing achieved <strong>300% growth this year</strong>, is forecast to deliver another <strong>100% growth next year</strong>, and is firmly on track to expand into a <strong>£100 million division within 5 years purely in co-manufacturing</strong>. Global powerhouse brands trust us under multi-year co-manufacturing agreements, validating our industry credibility, technical excellence, and manufacturing reliability.</p> <p><strong>About the Role</strong></p> <p>We are seeking a highly organised, proactive, and customer-focused <strong>Account Liaison Officer </strong>to join our fast-paced co-manufacturing division, reporting directly into the <strong>Commercial Director</strong>.</p> <p>In this role, you will serve as the primary operational conduit between our valued external co-manufacturing partners and internal site functions, including Production, Planning, Logistics, and Quality. You will drive day-to-day operational execution, clear customer communication, and end-to-end order tracking—ensuring customer forecasts, purchase orders, production timelines, and stock reconciliations run smoothly from inception through to dispatch.</p> <p><strong>As an Account Liaison Officer you will:</strong></p> <p><strong>Customer Liaison & Communication</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Operational Point of Contact:</strong> Act as the first port of call for day-to-day customer enquiries regarding production updates, lead times, batch progress, and dispatch schedules.</li> <li><strong>Customer Updates & Reviews:</strong> Prepare and participate in regular operational update calls with customers, providing transparent visibility on open order status and delivery milestones.</li> <li><strong>Cross-Functional Coordination:</strong> Collaborate closely with internal factory teams (Planning, Production, Materials Management, Quality, and Dispatch) to ensure client requirements are understood and executed smoothly.</li> <li><strong>Escalation Support:</strong> Promptly raise and track operational bottlenecks or supply chain escalations with internal stakeholders and the Commercial Director, keeping customers proactively informed of resolutions.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Demand, Supply & Production Coordination</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Demand Planning Interface:</strong> Collate customer demand forecasts and align them with internal planners to assess production line capacity and material requirements.</li> <li><strong>Supply Planning & OTIF Monitoring:</strong> Track component and raw material deliveries to support target On-Time, In-Full (OTIF) manufacturing schedules.</li> <li><strong>Production & Kitting Schedules:</strong> Liaise with site operational teams across our powder blending, bar, tableting, and fruit preparation plants to monitor kitting activities and scheduled production runs.</li> <li><strong>Supply Health Tracking:</strong> Support regular supply health and risk reporting, flagging potential raw material or component shortages before they impact production plans.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Order Processing & Systems Administration</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Order Processing:</strong> Accurately translate customer purchase orders into production and planning schedules across THG’s planning systems.</li> <li><strong>THG Ingenuity Systems:</strong> Raise, monitor, and coordinate production orders within THG’s proprietary Ingenuity platform.</li> <li><strong>B2B Portal & Price List Set-Up:</strong> Assist with setting up customer price lists on the THGB2B portal and ensure quarterly pricing uploads and system adjustments are maintained accurately in line with agreed terms.</li> <li><strong>New Product Range Administration:</strong> Assist in setting up initial reporting suites, tracking master SKU data, and ensuring data alignment for new product range introductions.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Inventory Reconciliation & Operational Control</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Free-Issued Stock Reconciliation:</strong> Perform regular reconciliations of customer-supplied (free-issued) raw materials, packaging, and ingredients, tracking usage, investigating discrepancies, and reporting remaining balances.</li> <li><strong>Finance & Timings Alignment:</strong> Provide timely order movement and production timing updates to the Commercial Director and Finance teams to support revenue tracking and month-end financial reviews.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What skills and experience do I need for this role?</strong></p> <p><strong>Essential Requirements</strong></p> <ul> <li>Previous experience in a customer service, client liaison, supply chain coordination, account coordination, or production administration role (ideally within FMCG, food & beverage, packaging, or manufacturing).</li> <li>Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to maintain clear, professional, and positive customer relationships.</li> <li>High accuracy in order processing, stock reconciliation, and maintaining system data.</li> <li>Basic understanding of production workflows, material lead times, and supply chain processes.</li> <li>Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Excel (pivot tables, lookups, reporting spreadsheets) and comfort working with ERP, MRP, or proprietary ordering portals.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Desirable Attributes</strong></p> <ul> <li>Prior experience working within contract manufacturing (co-man) or third-party client operations.</li> <li>Familiarity with food, nutrition, or pharmaceutical manufacturing standards (e.g., BRCGS, GMP).</li> </ul> <p><strong>Working Pattern & Office Locations</strong></p> <p>Collaboration and close proximity to our manufacturing plants are essential to our operational velocity. description: Who We Are At Partnerize, we're on a mission to transform the way businesses grow. We've built the leading partnership automation platform that empowers brands to discover, engage, and convert their audiences at scale. From affiliate marketing to influencer collaborations, we help our clients build and manage profitable partnerships that drive real results. We're a team of passionate problem-solvers who are dedicated to helping our clients win in the ever-evolving world of digital marketing. Why Join Us We're looking for passionate, talented people who want to be part of a winning team. At Partnerize, you'll find a culture of collaboration, innovation, and respect. We're guided by our core values, and we're committed to creating an environment where everyone can do their best work. We also offer a competitive salary, generous benefits, and a flexible work environment that allows you to thrive both personally and professionally. If you're ready to grow your career and make a difference, we'd love to hear from you. About the Role We're looking for a Senior DevOps Engineer to join our engineering team and champion the deployment architecture that drives our platform maturity. You'll be embedded within our engineering teams, optimizing day-to-day delivery across our on-premise estate while acting as the key engineering stakeholder to help shape, configure, and roll out our new Kubernetes platform, modernising how we deploy and scale workloads. This is a hands-on role with real impact. You won't be rubber-stamping tickets; you'll have true autonomy over our CI/CD pipelines, automated guardrails, and migration strategies, shaping how engineering safely and rapidly ships value to production. What You'll Be Doing BAU & Platform Stability Utilise and contribute to Ansible-based deployment automation to facilitate seamless product feature releases, adhering to established TechOps peer-review processes. Monitor application-level health within the cluster, collaborating with TechOps on incident response and driving post-mortems for engineering-led deployments. Maintain clear documentation, deployment runbooks, and developer self-service guides to streamline the engineering onboarding and release processes. Kubernetes Represent Engineering as a key stakeholder in platform design: Collaborate with TechOps to shape engineering self-service workflows, guardrails, and standards. This includes contributing requirements for Kubernetes primitives (such as Gateway API, RBAC, admission controllers, and resource policies) to ensure engineering teams can move fast safely, without compromising core platform stability. Standardise application-level configurations: Work alongside TechOps to establish clear engineering standards within the namespaces for ingress, RBAC, namespacing strategy, and secrets management. Drive phased application migrations: Partner with engineering teams to containerise and migrate existing workloads to Kubernetes, starting with non-critical environments to establish confidence before moving business-critical systems. Build robust deployment pipelines: Establish CI/CD workflows for Kubernetes-based deployments (using Helm, Kustomize, ArgoCD, or similar) with automated guardrails to ensure fast, repeatable, and safe code delivery. Implement application observability: Set up application-level metrics, logging, and alerting within the namespaces, ensuring engineering teams have the visibility they need to monitor workload health. Create developer self-service documentation: Document deployment runbooks, manifest templates, and best practices so that engineers can onboard and self-serve safely within the established guardrails. What We're Looking For Must-Have Strong interpersonal and communication skills : we're a people-first culture where teamwork is paramount. On highly technical projects with many moving parts, the ability to collaborate openly, communicate clearly, and bring people with you is just as important as technical ability Strong, demonstrable experience with Ansible : roles, inventories, vault, idempotency, the lot Comfortable with Docker and Docker Compose in production environments Understanding of networking fundamentals Strong scripting ability: Bash and Python Experience with GitOps tooling: ArgoCD or Flux Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager or equivalent) Ability to think creatively within constraints and plan pragmatically around them: our stack is real-world, not greenfield-perfect, and we need someone who can deliver iteratively, working with what exists today while roadmapping towards the ideal state A methodical, security-conscious approach Nice-to-Have Familiarity with Helm chart authoring and management Experience with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform (even in an on-prem context) Experience with secrets management tooling (HashiCorp Vault, Sealed Secrets, External Secrets Operator) Prior experience in a role where you balanced greenfield work alongside BAU responsibilities The Kind of Person We're After You're comfortable being the person engineering teams come to when something's on fire, and you're also comfortable saying "let me schedule that properly" when it isn't You can hold your own in a conversation with a software engineer, a network engineer, and senior leadership even if they all want different things You write things down. Runbooks and diagrams: you treat documentation as part of the job, not an afterthought You have opinions about how things should be done, but you're pragmatic; you know when to pick the right tool vs. the perfect tool Autonomously drive outcomes : we're looking for people who demonstrate intent and take initiative, not those who wait to be told what to do next What We Offer True ownership of the delivery lifecycle: The autonomy to shape how we ship code, build pipelines, and automate guardrails, moving entirely away from manual ticket execution. A pivotal role in our cloud-native transformation: The opportunity to act as the key engineering stakeholder shaping our migration to Kubernetes, partnering closely with TechOps to build a modern, scalable platform. A progressive engineering culture: A collaborative, forward-thinking team that values automation, continuous improvement, and building modern delivery standards. We welcome applications from candidates who don't tick every box. If you've got strong Ansible and Kubernetes experience and the right mindset, we'd love to hear from you. UK Benefits & Perks 25 days holiday in addition to bank holidays Enhanced Parental Leave: 6 months full pay for birth parent, 4 weeks non-birth parent at full pay after one year employment 5 extra 'Partnerize Parental Days' each year Private Medical and Dental Insurance Enhanced pension contributions Cycle to Work scheme Eye Care Vouchers Life Assurance Enhanced Wellness Program including access to EAP, Wellness Coaching & Wellness Programs Regular company events and activities Our Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion We are committed to attracting, developing, and advancing our outstanding team members, regardless of race, ethnic identity, sexual orientation, religion, age, gender, gender identity, physical abilities, or any other dimension of diversity. We strive to foster an environment where people can be their authentic selves, raise concerns and innovate, all without fear; where they are treated fairly and respectfully, have equal access to opportunities and resources and can contribute fully to the organization's success. Every individual in our business is expected to live this commitment without exception. Privacy and data protection . Please do not contact or forward resumes to our company employees or locations. Any unsolicited resumes will be considered Partnerize property. We love bringing people together in person, and that passion for great experiences extends to our employees as well. If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team. The Senior Event Production Manager (Planning) is responsible for overseeing the planning and execution of events, ensuring seamless coordination between clients and internal teams. Acting as the primary point of contact for clients throughout the planning process, this role ensures that all aspects of an event – from logistics and technical production to catering and on-site operations – are delivered to the highest standard. The role requires strong leadership, project management, and communication skills to ensure client expectations are met while maintaining operational efficiency. Key responsibilities: Team Leadership & Management Lead and manage the Events Team, ensuring effective staff scheduling and resource allocation. Conduct biannual appraisals and regular one-to-one meetings with direct reports, providing training and professional development plans. Ensure all team members adhere to company policies and procedures, including compliance with statutory Health & Safety training requirements. Maintain high standards of performance and service delivery within the team. Ensure strong cross-functional collaboration with other departments, including Sales and Operations. Oversee team performance management, including probation reviews, performance improvement plans, and disciplinary procedures where required. Events Planning & Coordination : Oversee the planning and execution of events across physical, hybrid, and virtual formats. Act as the main client liaison during the planning phase, ensuring clear communication and alignment with their requirements. Develop and maintain detailed event documentation, including Programme Execution Orders (PEOs), room layouts, event timelines, and client deliverables. Conduct client kick-off meetings, providing guidance on deadlines, requirements, and production schedules. Collaborate with internal teams, including AV production, catering, and operations, to finalise event logistics. Ensure all pre-event planning milestones are met, providing regular updates to stakeholders. Manage client expectations regarding event capabilities and work with Product and Design teams on potential platform improvements. Facilitate pre-event and post-event debriefs with internal teams and clients, ensuring continuous improvement. Operational Excellence: Work closely with the Sales Team to support pre-sales activities, advising on event feasibility, logistics, and timelines. Assist in the creation of event proposals, room diagrams, and other pre-sales materials. Oversee event budget management, ensuring accurate cost calculations, approvals, and final invoicing. Supervise on-site event operations, ensuring smooth execution and addressing any challenges in real time. Ensure the team adheres to company service standards and hospitality protocols at all times. Lead weekly event meetings and Programme Execution Order (PEO) discussions, ensuring alignment across all stakeholders. Skills & Experience Essential: Extensive experience in event planning and production, with a strong background in physical, hybrid, and virtual event formats. Proven leadership and team management experience. Strong organisational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple events simultaneously. As the business pushes forward with bold ambitions, the legal team’s purpose is clear: to drive Carwow’s growth with integrity and confidence – and that’s where you come in! YOUR MISSION We are a platform that sits right in the middle between consumers and OEMs/Dealers in the car-changing journey. Datasits at the heart of everything we do and we want to commercialise it responsibly. As Senior Privacy Counsel, you will be Carwow’s dedicated in-house privacy lawyer and operational privacy lead, playing a pivotal role in enabling the business to grow and scale at pace with integrity. This is an exciting opportunity to develop your career in a complex, high-growth and data-thirsty marketplace business. We are looking for a Senior Privacy Counsel who wants to do more than provide legal advice from the sidelines. We are not at “Day Zero”. We currently have an external DPO, established policies, templates, a RoPA and a risk register. We need a tech-fluent privacy lawyer who is equally comfortable advising and doing: someone who can interpret complex legal requirements, exercise sound legal judgement and provide pragmatic advice, but who will also roll up their sleeves and build, operate and continuously improve the mechanisms that make privacy work in practice. You will have the mandate to lift the lid on our technology stack, validate our data flows, identify legal and operational privacy risks and work directly with our Product, Engineering, Data, Marketing and commercial teams to keep the business safe and moving fast. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Privacy governance and framework development: Own, develop and maintain Carwow’s enterprise privacy governance framework, encompassing internal policies, ROPAs, privacy notices, risk registers, retention schedules and associated controls. Interpret applicable legal requirements and ensure our documentation and processes reflect the reality of Carwow’s technology stack and processing activities, leading remediation where discrepancies or risks are identified. Legal advice and business partnering: Act as Carwow’s principal in-house legal advisor on privacy and data protection matters. Develop strong business partnering relationships across Marketing, Media, Product, Engineering, Data and other parts of the business, providing pragmatic, risk-based legal advice that enables commercial objectives while appropriately managing privacy risk. Provide advice to senior management and support the General Counsel in updating the Company’s Senior Leadership Team and Executives as needed. Culture & Training: Build a strong internal perception of privacy as a “trust builder”. Design and deliver role-specific training that is engaging, commercially relevant and free of unnecessary legal jargon, helping teams understand both their legal obligations and how to apply them in practice. Breach response: Lead the privacy aspects of data breach and incident response, working cross-functionally to investigate incidents, assess legal and regulatory risk, determine notification obligations and oversee remediation. Liaise with the external DPO, regulators and other relevant stakeholders as appropriate. DPAs, DSAs and data contracting: Draft, review and negotiate DPAs, DSAs and other data protection provisions and agreements arising from commercial arrangements. Provide practical legal advice on controller/processor relationships, data sharing, international transfers and related privacy risks. DSARs and individual rights: Own and continuously improve Carwow’s processes for responding to data subject rights requests, ensuring requests can be handled lawfully, efficiently and with minimal disruption to the business. Provide legal guidance on complex or sensitive requests where required. Retail Media and Ad Tech: Provide legal and operational privacy support on new commercial propositions looking to leverage Carwow’s data for third-party audience targeting, segmentation and advertising. Advise on the appropriate use of personal data, profiling, consent and data-sharing structures and help design commercially workable and legally robust mechanisms for using and sharing data. Product, Data and Technology: Work closely with Data & Insights, IT, Engineering and Product teams throughout the product lifecycle to embed Privacy by Design. Lead or support privacy assessments, identify legal and operational risks in new products and processing activities, and translate complex technical data flows into clear, risk-based advice for the General Counsel, Executives and wider business. Operationalise Compliance: Own and operate core privacy compliance processes, including DPIAs, LIAs and data-sharing assessments. Look continuously for opportunities to integrate these into existing business workflows, with an eye on making compliance proportionate, scalable and automated wherever possible. Regulatory developments: Monitor and interpret relevant developments in privacy, data protection, digital regulation and related areas, assess their impact on Carwow and translate new legal requirements into practical changes to products, policies, controls and business processes. Corporate work: Provide privacy legal support on M&A, funding and other corporate transactions, including conducting privacy due diligence, identifying material risks and supporting remediation and integration activity. AI and emerging technology: Advise on the privacy implications of AI and emerging technologies adopted or developed across the business, while supporting the development of practical governance mechanisms that allow Carwow to innovate responsibly. Multi-jurisdictional: Support Carwow’s businesses across the UK, Germany, Spain and Portugal, advising on relevant local and European privacy requirements and working with external counsel where specialist local advice is required. KEY REQUIREMENTS A qualified lawyer, admitted to practise in England & Wales or another relevant UK or European jurisdiction, with significant experience advising on privacy and data protection matters. Significant experience working in-house, balancing legal and regulatory requirements with commercial objectives and operating as a trusted advisor to the business. Strong working knowledge of UK and European data protection law, with the ability to interpret legislation, regulatory guidance and emerging issues and translate them into clear, practical and commercially workable advice. Experience not only providing privacy legal advice but also building, operating or materially contributing to a privacy programme, including areas such as DPIAs, RoPAs, privacy notices, data rights, retention, incident response and privacy governance. The ability and willingness to work autonomously as Carwow’s principal in-house privacy specialist, moving comfortably between complex legal analysis and hands-on operational delivery. Passionate about the intersection of AI and privacy, with an interest in how to safeguard the organisation during technology adoption while also leveraging AI to enhance and automate privacy operations. A team player with a growth mindset, high EQ and low ego, excited to be part of a scale-up, high-growth company where every day brings new challenges and opportunities. To be able to work in a fast-paced environment with teams that move and pivot quickly. Fluency in English and strong written and verbal communication skills, together with a proactive, persuasive and adaptable manner. Driven to ensure the Legal & Compliance Team is viewed as a genuine partner to the business, with the initiative and credibility to build relationships across functions and at senior levels. Ability to lead cross-functional projects and influence stakeholders without relying on formal authority. A track record of working effectively with all levels of an organisation, including senior management and executives. BONUS POINTS Experience working in a tech platform or marketplace environment. Experience in Mar-Tech or Ad-Tech. Experience in the automotive industry. Experience advising on AI governance or wider digital regulation. Experience supporting organisations operating across multiple European jurisdictions. A CIPP/E and/or CIPM qualification from the IAPP, or equivalent demonstrable privacy expertise. INTERVIEW PROCESS Introductory call with our Talent team. Interview with our Director of Legal and another member of our Legal Team. Interview with our General Counsel Carwow Values interview with 2 x members of the Carwow business. title: People Partner Lead, Corporate Functions, Product & Tech
description: Mission Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives. About Neko Health Neko Health is a Swedish healthcare technology company founded in 2018 by Hjalmar Nilsonne and Daniel Ek. Our mission is to redesign healthcare by shifting the focus from reactive treatment to proactive and preventive care. We are building a new kind of healthcare experience designed to help people stay ahead of their health. By combining medical expertise with breakthrough technology, we make it possible to quickly and non-invasively gather a broad picture of a person's health and deliver clear insights within minutes. Headquartered in Stockholm and New York, Neko Health offers the Neko Body Scan experience across Europe and the US, supported by a growing team of people working to transform how healthcare is delivered. Why this role exists Legal, Finance and People are what let Neko operate, hire and stay compliant as it scales, and Product & Technology is the largest, most complex function at HQ. These aren't the same kind of problem. Each function sits at a different stage of maturity, and this role isn't about pulling them into one shape. It's about moving fluidly between genuinely different disciplines, bringing the right kind of people practice to each, rather than defaulting to a single playbook. This is one of the most senior People roles at HQ outside the Global People Lead itself. It suits a senior level HR operator who's genuinely comfortable holding several different kinds of problem at once, and who brings real depth in organisational design, workforce planning, strategy and culture, genuine command of each rather than surface-level familiarity. What you'll do Own the people agenda across Corporate Functions and partners with the Global People lead on parts of the Product & Tech organisation Lead workforce planning and organisational design across Legal, Finance, People, (and support to parts of the Product & Technology teams) role clarity, resourcing decisions and structural recommendations tailored to each function's stage Meet each function on its own terms, building where a function is still finding its shape, optimising where it's stable, rather than applying one approach everywhere Build genuine partnership with the leaders who run each of these teams, calibrating the relationship to what each one needs Be the strategic partner to senior leadership Serve as the primary strategic partner across Legal, Finance, People and some of the Product & Technology teams, translating business strategy into people priorities, programmes and operating plans for each function Coach and challenge leaders on the decisions that shape the organisation they'll be running next year, thinking a step ahead of today's priorities Bring sound judgement and discretion to the most sensitive people matters across all four functions Champion Neko's culture and Vitals Partner with leaders across Legal, Finance, People and parts of the Product & Technology to embed Neko's cultural Vitals into how their teams actually operate, day to day Help leaders translate the Vitals into practical behaviours and decisions across genuinely different functions Build the rituals and feedback loops that keep culture genuinely lived as each function matures at its own pace Drive talent management across Corporate Functions and Product & Tech Working in partnership with the Growth & Engagement team to drive leadership development, performance and engagement for the leadership population across Legal, Finance, People and Product & Technology Advise on compensation, mobility and promotions in partnership with Reward & Enablement, ensuring internal equity and market competitiveness across genuinely different functions Lead change and manage risk Lead and sponsor change initiatives that affect structure or operating model in any of these functions, owning scope, timeline, stakeholder engagement and change readiness from start to finish Manage employee relations matters across Legal, Finance, People and Product & Technology, working directly with Legal colleagues and specialist counsel to resolve issues with discretion and confidentiality Spot risk early, whether that's capacity strain in Legal or Finance, or Product & Technology's pace outstripping its structure Drive organisational design and workforce planning Use workforce and org data to shape decisions ahead of need Deliver people analytics and actionable insights that turn data into clear, decision-ready recommendations Put data and AI to work in how the people agenda runs day to day, sharper decisions, less manual effort Bring the right practice to functions at different stages Recognise that Legal, Finance, People and Product & Technology each need different structures, rhythms and support, and build accordingly Turn central People programmes into practice that fits each function's actual culture and maturity Experience evaluating how AI informs talent decisions and org design, bringing the judgement to design with AI as a genuine participant in how roles and structures should look, actively shaping the work itself. What you bring Deep, hands-on experience across organisational design, workforce planning, people strategy and culture, genuine depth in all four, built through direct ownership rather than generalist HRBP exposure 10+ years in senior HR Business Partner, People Partner, or People/HR leadership roles, including ownership of the people agenda across genuinely different functions at Director level or above Experience owning leadership development and performance calibration outcomes for a senior leadership population A track record of personally leading change initiatives end to end: scope, timeline, and stakeholder engagement A genuine passion for culture and values, with experience helping leaders embed them into how their teams actually work A track record of partnering with and influencing senior functional leaders on complex, high-stakes organisational decisions, operating with genuine autonomy as an independent decision-maker Comfort holding functions at very different stages of maturity at once, adapting approach rather than applying one framework to all Fluent with people data and actively using AI in your own work Working knowledge of employment law relevant to Neko's HQ locations, with the judgement to know when to bring in specialist expertise About Titles at Neko We use a simplified internal title framework that prioritises clarity over hierarchy, so internal titles may differ from market-facing role titles. Scope, impact and level of the role are fully aligned and will be clearly discussed throughout the process. Hiring Process Candidates progress from application and structured screening through thoughtfully designed interviews, culminating in a formal offer and final pre-employment checks before joining the team. Equal Opportunity & Inclusion Statement Neko Health is committed to inclusive hiring and member-first care. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and encourage you to request reasonable adjustments to support your application. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Research Sonographer
description: Mission Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives. Role Purpose We’re looking for an experienced Ultrasound sonographer to join our multidisciplinary team in London on a 12 month fixed term contract and help to take ultrasounds as part of a clinical research study. This is a key role focused on delivering high-quality, independent assessments. You’ll perform and interpret ultrasound scans of adult women who are receiving a breast ultrasound as part of a clinical study. You will work in conjunction with the principal investigator of the study to ensure that assessments and reports are of research-grade quality. This is a fixed term role that lasts for the duration of the study and is based at our clinics in London. What You’ll Deliver Perform high-quality diagnostic ultrasound examinations in line with clinical guidelines and best practices with focus on breast ultrasound Pass on the study-specific acquisition and interpretation qualification task before performing study scans, with certificate filed in the investigational site file. Independently interpret and report ultrasound findings, ensuring timely delivery of results that are uploaded to a standardised electronic case report form. Collaborate with our multidisciplinary research team to help deliver Neko’s clinical trial focused on better understanding risks of breast cancer. Adherence to the study acquisition SOP Equipment QA maintenance logged on-site. Liaise directly with the study PI and research team where needed. Minimum Requirements HCPC-registered diagnostic radiographer (or other HCPC-/NMC-registered healthcare professional), holding a CASE-accredited postgraduate qualification in breast ultrasound (PgCert / PgDip / MSc, or a named CASE-accredited breast ultrasound module. Documented, current breast ultrasound practice, with a minimum of two years’ full-time-equivalent breast scanning. Advanced radiographic experience of reporting autonomously within the NHS Breast Screening Programme (NHSBSP) or an equivalent quality-assurance framework . Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex information clearly to study participants. Commitment to maintaining high clinical standards and engaging in ongoing professional development. Preferred Experience with previous ultrasound scanning as part of clinical trials Experience with shear-wave elastography acquisition and reporting. Experience with Philips US machines, and decision support software Familiarity with data entry as part of clinical research studies. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: Our mission We're making Africa the first cashless continent. In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. Wave is very transparent, whether that's defaulting to public conversations in slack, frequent Ask Wave Anything sessions, or defaulting to writing public docs to explain major decisions. Major benefits: Subsidized health insurance for you and your dependents and retirement contributions (both vary from country to country). 6 months of fully paid parental leave and subsidized fertility assistance. Flexible vacation, with most folks taking between 21-30 days exclusive of statutory holidays. $10,000 annual charitable donation matching. Along the way you'll meet our CEO, Head of People, Head of Product, both Engineering Directors, and a senior leader from one of our markets. Clear, short, and persuasive, for readers who aren't engineers.
